perturbed_solution:
The given ratio tells us that $\frac{b}{a}=3$ or that $b=3a$. We substitute this value for $a$ so we have an equation with only one variable. We find
\begin{align*}
3a&=12+5a \\
\Rightarrow \quad -2a&=12 \\
\Rightarrow \quad a &= 6 \\
\Rightarrow \quad a &= \boxed{6}.
\end{align*}

errors.rationale: The equation b=3a gives an expression for b, so it must be substituted for b in b=12-5a, not for a; substituting for a misidentifies the variable being eliminated.
After substituting b=3a into b=12-5a, the right side must stay 12-5a. Changing the subtraction to addition alters the sign of the 5a term.
From -2a=12, dividing both sides by -2 gives a=-6, not a=6; the negative sign must be retained.
